name: Duloxetine
sections: White to slightly brownish powder (hydrochloride), slightly soluble in water.

Created by Eli Lilly researchers including David Wong, co-inventor of fluoxetine; the (+)-S-enantiomer was selected for its greater serotonin reuptake inhibition. First approval/introduction: US FDA and EU 2004 (Eli Lilly and Company).

Potent inhibitor of neuronal serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake, weak dopamine reuptake inhibitor. Antidepressant effect and enhancement of descending inhibitory pain pathways underlie its use in depression, anxiety and chronic pain states. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits SERT (Ki 0.7–0.8 nM) and NET (Ki 7.5 nM) with negligible affinity for dopaminergic, cholinergic, histaminergic or adrenergic receptors.
Summary: Delayed absorption (enteric-coated); Tmax ~6 h. >90% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP1A2 and CYP2D6. Half-life ~12 h.
Chronic musculoskeletal pain (chronic low back pain, osteoarthritis knee pain)
MDD: 40–60 mg/day (20–30 mg twice daily or 60 mg once daily); max 120 mg/day
GAD: start 30 mg once daily for 1 week, then 60 mg once daily; max 120 mg/day
Diabetic neuropathic pain / fibromyalgia / musculoskeletal pain: 30 mg once daily for 1 week, then 60 mg once daily
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Taper over at least 2 weeks when stopping
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Avoid in any hepatic impairment or substantial alcohol use.
Start 30 mg once daily; monitor for hyponatraemia and falls.
Approved for GAD (7–17 y) and fibromyalgia (13–17 y) in some regions; monitor for suicidality and growth.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; late-pregnancy exposure may cause neonatal adaptation syndrome and increases postpartum haemorrhage risk.
Excreted in breast milk; not recommended.
Use with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitors
Severe hepatic impairment; severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min)
Concomitant fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin or enoxacin (strong CYP1A2 inhibitors)
Suicidality in children, adolescents and young adults
Hepatotoxicity – avoid in heavy alcohol use or chronic liver disease
Discontinuation syndrome – taper gradually; activation of mania
Nausea (most common), dry mouth, constipation, decreased appetite
MAOIs, linezolid, triptans, tramadol, other serotonergic drugs (serotonin syndrome)
With or without food; avoid heavy alcohol (liver injury).
Blood pressure; LFTs if symptoms; sodium in elderly; mood/suicidality early in treatment.
Somnolence, serotonin syndrome, seizures, vomiting, tachycardia. Supportive care; activated charcoal.
Cipriani et al., Lancet 2018 – network meta-analysis of 21 antidepressants: duloxetine more effective than placebo.
Goldstein et al., Pain 2005 – duloxetine 60–120 mg/day significantly reduced diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain.
Skljarevski et al., 2010 – efficacy in chronic low back pain.
Swallow whole – do not crush or open
Do not stop suddenly – dizziness, irritability may occur
Report worsening mood or suicidal thoughts
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
